74731.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74731.question_text: Whose sons treated the offering of the Lord with contempt
74731.explanation:
According to the biblical account in 1 Samuel 2, Eli was the High Priest of Israel, but his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were described as "wicked men" who had no regard for the Lord.

When people came to offer sacrifices, Eli’s sons would take the best meat for themselves by force before the fat was even burned as an offering to God. Their behaviour caused people to abhor making offerings to the Lord because the process had become corrupt.  In addition to mishandling the offerings, they were also known for acting immorally at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

Because Eli failed to restrain his sons, a prophecy was given that his family line would be cut off from the priesthood, and both Hophni and Phinehas died on the same day during a battle with the Philistines.

74732.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74732.question_text: Daniel was cast into the den of lions because he
74732.explanation:
According to the biblical account in Daniel 6, Daniel was cast into the den of lions because he continued to pray to God despite a royal decree forbidding it.

It is important to note, however, that Daniel did not hide his actions. Jealous officials tricked King Darius into signing an irrevocable law that, for 30 days, anyone who prayed to any god or man other than the king would be thrown to the lions.

When Daniel learned of the law, he went home to his upstairs room and prayed with his windows open toward Jerusalem, just as he had always done. Rather than hiding (which would have been cowardice) or making a public spectacle (which would have been pride), he simply maintained his usual spiritual discipline in a visible way. His enemies, who were watching him, caught him in the act of praying and reported him to the king to force the execution of the law.

74733.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74733.question_text: Moses took the bones of Joseph during the exodus because
74733.explanation:
Before Joseph died in Egypt, he made the "sons of Israel" swear that they would carry his bones out of Egypt when God eventually came to lead them to the Promised Land. This request was seen as an act of faith; Joseph believed God's promise that his descendants would one day return to the land of Canaan.

Even though hundreds of years had passed, Moses remembered this responsibility and ensured the oath was honoured during the rapid departure from Egypt.

options.text: it was their custom to carry all bones
Joseph had sworn that they should carry the bones
the bones were so precious to the Israelites

74734.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74734.question_text: The team that Cornelius sent to bring Peter from Joppa consist of
74734.explanation:
According to Acts, after receiving a vision from an angel instructing him to send for Peter in Joppa, Cornelius immediately assembled this small team to carry out the task. Cornelius called two of his own servants who lived in his home. He also chose a "devout" soldier from among his personal attendants. This soldier was noted for his own piety and religious devotion.

Cornelius explained everything that had happened in his vision to these three men before sending them on to Joppa.

74735.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74735.question_text: The three disciples that witnessed the Transfiguration of Jesus were
74735.explanation: This event is recorded in Matthew 17:1, Mark 9:2 and Luke 9:28. Jesus took this specific "inner circle" of three disciples up onto a high mountain, where He was transfigured before them, His face shining like the sun and His clothes becoming white as light.

74736.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74736.question_text:
...the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie...

In the above statement about Jesus, John the Baptist displayed great
74736.explanation: This statement is recorded in John 1:27. By saying he was not even worthy to untie the strap (thong) of Jesus' sandals—a task usually reserved for the lowest of slaves—John the Baptist was displaying extreme humility and acknowledging Jesus' superior status and divine authority.

74737.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74737.question_text: Before Jesus ascended into Heaven, He asked His disciples to remain in Jerusalem, which showed He
74737.explanation: In Acts 1:4-5, Jesus commanded His disciples not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for "the promise of the Father"—the Holy Spirit. He wanted them to be "baptized with the Holy Spirit" and empowered before they began their mission to preach the Gospel to the ends of the earth.

options.text: wanted them to replace Judas Iscariot
wanted them to prepare before proceeding on missions
expected them to avoid persecution from the Gentiles
did not want them to preach to non-Jews

74738.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74738.question_text: According to the teachings on justification by faith, who was the one man whose obedience brought righteousness to the world?
74738.explanation: In Romans 5:18-19, Paul contrasts Adam with Jesus. He explains that while Adam's disobedience brought sin, Jesus' one act of obedience brought righteousness and life to all.

74739.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74739.question_text: According to Peter, a Christian should exercise his freedom by
74739.explanation: In 1 Peter 2:16, Peter instructs Christians to live as free people, but not to use their freedom as a "cover-up for evil". Instead, they are to use that freedom to serve God by doing what is right.

options.text: using it as a pretext for evil

74740.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74740.question_text: Those who are not qualified for a place in the Kingdom of God include:
74740.explanation: This aligns with 1 Corinthians 6:9-10, where Paul lists several behaviours that disqualify individuals from inheriting the kingdom of God, specifically mentioning idolaters, those who practice sexual immorality (fornicators) and the greedy.

74741.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74741.question_text: According to Paul in Galatians, Christians have become children of God through
74741.explanation: In Galatians 3:26, Paul writes, "So in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith". He argues that it is faith, not adherence to the law, that brings people into God's family.

options.text: subjecting themselves to the rule of law

74742.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74742.question_text:
I will faithfully give them their recompense, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.

The above statement of the LORD to Israel in Isiah's prophecy suggests
74742.explanation: The promise in Isaiah 61:8 of a "faithful recompense" and an "everlasting covenant" is a message of hope and restoration for a people who had suffered.

74743.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74743.question_text: Baal worship was introduced in Israel by
74743.explanation:
According to the accounts in 1 Kings, Jezebel was a Phoenician princess, the daughter of Ethbaal, King of Tyre. When she married King Ahab of Israel, she brought her own prophets of Baal and Asherah into the royal court.

She influenced Ahab to build a temple and an altar for Baal in the capital city of Samaria. She famously attempted to eliminate the prophets of God, leading to the major confrontation between the prophet Elijah and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.

74744.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74744.question_text: The restrictions of Ezekiel's mission to the house of Israel were to show God's
74744.explanation:
When Ezekiel was called to be a "watchman" for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3:17), God imposed several symbolic restrictions and specific instructions on him. These restrictions, such as being struck mute for a time and being bound by cords, highlighted God's unwavering resolve and persistent nature. Despite Israel's rebellion and "hard-heartedness," God remained constant in His message and His presence among the exiles.

 Ezekiel’s silence and physical constraints were signs to the house of Israel. They demonstrated that even when communication seemed "restricted," God's plan was still actively unfolding.

74745.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74745.question_text: The parable of the drag net, according to Jesus, was to teach His listeners about the
74745.explanation:
The parable of the dragnet (Matthew 13:47-50) is one of the "Kingdom Parables" Jesus used to explain spiritual realities. Jesus explicitly explained that the sorting of "good" and "bad" fish represents the judgment at the end of the age. Just as fishermen sort fish on the shore, Jesus stated that "the angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous".

The parable concludes with the "bad" being thrown into a "furnace of fire". This is a symbol of the final day of reckoning for all humanity.

options.text: judgement at the close of age

74746.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74746.question_text: Abraham was referred to as a friend of God because he
74746.explanation:
When God commanded Abraham to leave his home or later to sacrifice his son, Isaac, Abraham did not argue or look for excuses. He trusted God completely and obeyed "on that very day".

The Scripture (James 2:23) notes that "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and because of this deep relationship of trust and obedience, he was called the Friend of God.

74747.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74747.question_text: The statement "when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing" warns against
74747.explanation:
In Matthew 6:1-4, Jesus warns against performing righteous deeds to be seen by others. Jesus specifically condemns "hypocrites" who blow trumpets in the synagogues and streets to attract attention to their charity.

 The phrase "do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing" is a command for secrecy and humility. Jesus teaches that those who seek human praise have already received their full reward, whereas those who give in secret will be rewarded by God.

options.text: letting friends know we are giving alms
giving alms in the public space
blowing trumpets when we give alms
letting people see us when giving alms

74748.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74748.question_text: Jonah, in his plots to escape from the presence of God, boarded a ship at Joppa to
74748.explanation:
In the Book of Jonah, when God commanded the prophet to go to Nineveh, Jonah attempted to flee in the opposite direction. He went down to the port city of Joppa and paid the fare for a ship bound for Tarshish to "flee from the presence of the Lord".

Tarshish was likely in modern-day Spain, representing the furthest known point in the opposite direction from Nineveh (modern-day Iraq).

74749.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74749.question_text: Jesus changed water to wine at Cana to Galilee to
74749.explanation: According to the Gospel of John, the turning of water into wine at the wedding feast in Cana was the first of Jesus' "signs". The primary purpose, as stated in John 2:11, was to reveal His glory. As a direct result of this miraculous sign, the text notes that "His disciples believed in Him".

options.text: meet the needs of the people
manifest his glory and make the disciples believe in him

74750.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74750.question_text: The Mission of the Seventy signifies mission to
74750.explanation: In the Gospel of Luke, Jesus sends out seventy (or seventy-two) disciples to prepare the way for Him.  In Jewish tradition, 70 was the number of the nations of the world (from Genesis 10). While the "Twelve" often symbolised a mission to the twelve tribes of Israel, the "Seventy" signifies the universal reach of the Gospel to the Gentiles and all nations.

74751.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74751.question_text: In his letter to the Colossians, Paul taught that when parents provoke their children, they ( children) become
74751.explanation: In Colossians 3:21, the Apostle Paul provides a specific warning to fathers (parents). "Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged". Paul taught that overbearing or harsh parenting could crush a child's spirit. This emphasises the need for encouragement within the family unit.

74752.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74752.question_text: On which day of the week did the appearance of Jesus take place
74752.explanation: Jesus rose from the dead on the first day of the week (Sunday). His initial appearances to Mary Magdalene and the disciples in the upper room occurred on that same first day.

74753.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74753.question_text: When Jesus told the would-be disciple who wanted to bury his father to leave the dead to bury their own dead, he meant that
74753.explanation: When a potential follower asked to first bury his father, Jesus replied, "Leave the dead to bury their own dead" (Matthew 8:22). This difficult saying was meant to emphasise the absolute priority of the Kingdom of God. It teaches that true discipleship entails detachment from even the most significant family obligations if they hinder one's immediate response to God's call.

options.text: this was an assurance of resurrection for all
discipleship entails detachment from the family
the man's father had not died
the spiritually dead should be left to bury the physically dead

74754.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74754.question_text: The Spiritual Gifts identified in first Corinthians include
74754.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 12, Paul identifies specific spiritual gifts, including wisdom, faith, healing, and prophecy.

options.text: love, joy, peace and long suffering

74755.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74755.question_text:
Have you killed and also taken possession?

The above statement by Prophet Elijah was addressed to
74755.explanation:
This statement comes from 1 Kings 21. It refers to the incident involving Naboth’s Vineyard.  King Ahab wanted a vineyard belonging to a man named Naboth, but Naboth refused to sell his ancestral inheritance.

Ahab's wife, Queen Jezebel, orchestrated a plot to have Naboth falsely accused of blasphemy and stoned to death so the King could take the land.

After Ahab went to take possession of the vineyard, God sent the Prophet Elijah to confront him. Elijah met him and delivered God's judgment, starting with the rhetorical question: "Have you killed and also taken possession?" (1 Kings 21:19).

74756.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74756.question_text:
Jesus spoke to them, saying: "I am the light of the world, whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life".

From the above statement, Jesus was trying to explain the importance in Christians'
74756.explanation:
The quote, "I am the light of the world, whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life," is found in John 8:12.

Jesus uses the metaphor of "light" to represent divine truth and guidance. "Light" represents the spiritual truth and the presence of God, while "darkness" represents sin, ignorance, and separation from God.

By following this "light," a person gains the "light of life," which refers to the spiritual understanding (knowledge of God) that guides a believer away from the death of sin and toward eternal life (salvation).

options.text: the knowledge of God, leading to salvation

74757.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74757.question_text: Where did Joshua deliver his farewell address to the Israelites?
74757.explanation:
This event is recorded in Joshua 24. Near the end of his life, Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem for a final covenant renewal. Shechem was a deeply symbolic place for the Israelites, as it was where God first promised the land to Abraham.

Joshua reviewed God's faithfulness to the nation and famously challenged the people to choose whom they would serve, stating, "But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord" (Joshua 24:15).

74758.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74758.question_text:
...he who touches the earth and it melts...?

Who was Prophet Amos referring to in the statement above?
74758.explanation:
The statement "...he who touches the earth and it melts..." is a direct quote from Amos 9:5. In this passage, the Prophet Amos uses powerful imagery to describe the supreme authority and awesome power of God:

The verse explicitly names the subject as "The Lord GOD of hosts" (or "The Lord, the LORD Almighty" in some translations). The term "hosts" refers to God as the commander of heavenly armies.

The "melting" of the earth symbolises that creation itself cannot stand before God's presence or judgment. Even the firmest ground is described as liquefying or quaking at His mere touch.

Amos uses this description to remind the Israelites that no one can hide or escape from God's judgment, as He has complete control over the entire universe.

74759.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74759.question_text: David spared the life of Saul but took away his
74759.explanation:
This took place in the Wilderness of Ziph. While King Saul and his army were sleeping, David and Abishai crept into Saul’s camp. Abishai wanted to kill Saul with his own spear, but David refused to harm "the Lord’s anointed."

Instead of killing him, David took Saul’s spear and the jar of water that were near his head as proof that he had the chance to take the King's life but chose mercy instead.

74760.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74760.question_text:
"No church entered into partnership with me in giving and receiving except only you"

The above statement of Paul was meant for the
74760.explanation:
In Philippians 4:15, Paul wrote this letter to the church at Philippi to thank them for their consistent financial and material support during his missionary journeys and his imprisonment. Paul specifies that this unique partnership began "in the early days of your acquaintance with the gospel, when I set out from Macedonia."

 While Paul supported himself through tentmaking to avoid being a burden, he accepted the gifts from the Philippians because they were sent out of love and a shared commitment to the ministry.

74761.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74761.question_text: Paul adjoins believers in Corinthians to forgive one another so that
74761.explanation: This instruction is found in 2 Corinthians 2:10-11. Paul encourages the church to forgive and comfort an individual who had caused grief to the community. He explains that forgiveness is necessary "in order that Satan might not outwit us; for we are not unaware of his schemes." Paul's concern was that bitterness or lack of mercy would create a foothold for spiritual division within the church.

options.text: Satan will not gain advantage over us

74762.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74762.question_text: According to the prophecy of Ezekiel, all souls belong to
74762.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 18:4: "Behold, all souls are mine; the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is mine...". In this chapter, God uses the prophet Ezekiel to explain individual accountability, making it clear that every human life is His creation and under His authority.

74763.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74763.question_text: The women of Samaria were described by Amos as
74763.explanation: In Amos 4:1, the prophet uses this metaphor to rebuke the wealthy women of Samaria. Bashan was a region known for its lush pastures and well-fed livestock; Amos used the term to criticise the women for their luxury, greed and oppression of the poor.

74764.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74764.question_text: Josiah's reward for being penitent and remorseful when Judah sinned against the LORD by worshipping other gods was
74764.explanation: In 2 Kings 22:18–20 and 2 Chronicles 34:26–28, the prophetess Huldah delivers a message from God to King Josiah. Because his heart was "tender and penitent," God promised that the disaster coming upon Jerusalem would not happen during his lifetime; instead, he would be "gathered to [his] grave in peace" and his eyes would not see the evil brought upon the place.

options.text: he was not going to witness the desolation
he was going to rebuild the Temple
Judah shall no longer be destroyed
his family will be saved from the forthcoming pestilence

74765.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74765.question_text:
"You pity the plant, for which you did not labour, nor did you make it grow which came into being in a night, and perished in a night".

The statment above was directed to
74765.explanation: This is found in Jonah 4:10. After Jonah became angry that God spared the city of Nineveh, God used a fast-growing plant that withered overnight to teach him a lesson about compassion. God's point was that if Jonah could feel pity for a plant he didn't even grow, God should certainly have compassion for a great city filled with people.

74766.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74766.question_text: In Jeremiah, the sovereignty of God is symbolised in the
74766.explanation: In Jeremiah 18:1–6, God instructs the prophet to go to a potter's house. Seeing the potter reshape a marred vessel on the wheel served as a visual parable. It demonstrated that just as a potter has absolute authority over the clay, God has the sovereign right to shape, break, or rebuild nations and individuals according to His will.

74767.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74767.question_text: In the book of Prophet Jeremiah, God promised to write the New Covenant on
74767.explanation: This prophecy is found in Jeremiah 31:33. Unlike the old covenant written on stone tablets, God promised a new era where He would put His law within His people and write it on their hearts, leading to a direct, personal relationship with Him.

74768.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
74768.question_text:
What was the answer of Jesus to Pilate's question?

"Are you the King of the Jews?"
74768.explanation: Recorded in Matthew 27:11, Mark 15:2, and Luke 23:3, Jesus gives this brief affirmation when questioned by the Roman governor.

75607.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75607.question_text: Who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
75607.explanation: Luke 19:4 records Zacchaeus climbing the tree because he was short.

75609.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75609.explanation: "Messiah" comes from Hebrew and means the one anointed by God to save His people.

75611.question_text: What did Jesus say about judging others?

options.text: Judge not, lest you be judged

75612.explanation: Genesis 40:20–21 shows the chief butler restored to his position, as Joseph had interpreted.

75614.question_text: Who told Pharaoh about Joseph's ability to interpret dreams?
75614.explanation: Genesis 41:9–13 recounts the cupbearer remembering Joseph's gift.

75617.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75617.question_text: What did Jesus use to feed the 5,000?
75617.explanation: Matthew 14:17–21 narrates that Jesus multiplied five loaves and two fish to feed the crowd.

75618.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75618.question_text: What did Paul experience on the road to Damascus?
75618.explanation: Acts 9:3–5 tells of Jesus appearing to Saul, leading to his conversion.

75620.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75620.question_text: Who wrote the Acts of the Apostles?
75620.explanation: Acts 1:1–2 reveals the author is the same as Luke's Gospel.

75622.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75622.explanation: Matthew 4:21 identifies James and John as sons of Zebedee and Jesus' disciples.

75623.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75623.question_text: What happened to the tower of Babel builders?
75623.explanation: Genesis 11:7–9 records that God confused their language, scattering them.

75624.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75624.question_text: What did Joseph interpret Pharaoh's dream to mean?
75624.explanation: Genesis 41:25–30 shows Joseph interpreting the dream about the fat and lean cows.

options.text: Seven years of abundance followed by famine

75625.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75625.question_text: How many days did Jesus fast in the wilderness?
75625.explanation: Matthew 4:2 shows Jesus fasted forty days and nights before being tempted by Satan.

75626.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75626.question_text: What vision did Peter see before meeting Cornelius?
75626.explanation: Acts 10:11–16 describes Peter's vision preparing him to accept Gentiles.

75628.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75628.question_text: What did the Israelites eat in the wilderness?
75628.explanation: Exodus 16: 13-15 describes God providing manna and quail during their journey

75629.question_text: Why was Moses forbidden from entering the Promised Land?
75629.explanation: Numbers 20:12 shows God's judgment because Moses disobeyed by striking instead of speaking.

options.text: He refused to speak to Pharaoh
He struck the rock in anger

75631.explanation: Numbers 20:12 shows God's judgment because Moses disobeyed by striking instead of speaking.

options.text: He refused to speak to Pharaoh
He struck the rock in anger

75633.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75633.question_text: What was the main message of John the Baptist?
75633.explanation: Matthew 3:2 records John's central message calling people to repentance.

options.text: Repent for the kingdom of God is at hand

75634.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75634.question_text: Who built the first temple in Jerusalem?
75634.explanation: 1 Kings 6 describes Solomon constructing the temple that David had planned.

75635.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75635.question_text: What did Jesus say is the second greatest commandment?
75635.explanation: Matthew 22:39 names this as second after loving God.

75637.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75637.question_text: What river did Jesus get baptised in?
75637.explanation: Matthew 3:13 confirms Jesus was baptised by John in the Jordan River.

75638.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75638.question_text: What river did Jesus get baptised in?
75638.explanation: Matthew 3:13 confirms Jesus was baptised by John in the Jordan River.

75639.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75639.explanation: Judges 16:18–21 shows Delilah coaxed Samson's secret and enabled his capture.

75640.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75640.explanation: Genesis 22: 11-12 shows God's angel stopping Abraham from killing Isaac.

75641.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

75642.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75642.question_text: How many plagues did God send on Egypt?
75642.explanation: Exodus chapters 7–12 list ten plagues sent to convince Pharaoh to release Israel.

75643.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75643.question_text: What miracle did Elisha perform for the Shunammite woman's son?
75643.explanation: 2 Kings 4:32–35 tells how Elisha revived the boy after he died.

75644.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75644.question_text: Who was the mother of Samuel the prophet?
75644.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:20 shows that Hannah, after praying earnestly to God, gave birth to Samuel.

75645.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75645.question_text: Who anointed Saul as the first king of Israel?
75645.explanation: 1 Samuel 10 describes the prophet Samuel anointing Saul as king.

75646.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75646.question_text: Who accused Naboth falsely to seize his vineyard?
75646.explanation: 1 Kings 21: 7-13 shows Jezebel arranging false witnesses to have Naboth killed.

75647.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75647.question_text: What is the significance of the veil tearing at Jesus' death?
75647.explanation: Matthew 27:51 symbolises that believers now have direct access to God

75648.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75648.question_text: What did Elisha use to purify the water at Jericho?
75648.explanation: In 2 Kings 2: 21, Elisha threw salt into the spring to heal the water.

75649.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75649.question_text: Who prophesied the coming of Elijah before the great day of the Lord?
75649.explanation: Malachi 4:5 foretells Elijah's coming before the Day of the Lord.

75650.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75650.explanation: While several authors contributed, King David wrote the majority of the Psalms.

75651.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75651.question_text: What did Jesus do at the Last Supper?
75651.explanation: John 13: 4-5 shows Jesus washing their feet as a symbol of humility

75652.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75652.question_text: Who was the king who asked for wisdom?
75652.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9 shows Solomon requesting wisdom to rule the people.

75653.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75653.explanation: Acts 2: 1-4 shows the Spirit filling believers with tongues and power.

75654.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75654.explanation: Acts 18:3 states Paul worked as a tentmaker to support himself.

75655.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75655.explanation: Matthew 21:7 depicts Jesus riding a donkey to fulfil prophecy.

75656.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75656.question_text: What did Jesus say about paying taxes?
75656.explanation: Matthew 22:21 shows Jesus' response to the legitimacy of civil obligations.

options.text: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's

75657.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75657.question_text: What did Paul compare the Church to in 1 Corinthians 12?
75657.explanation: Paul describes the church as one body with many parts (1 Corinthians 12:12–27).

75658.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75658.explanation: Matthew 1:23 says Emmanuel means "God is with us."

75659.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75659.explanation: 1 Samuel 2: 34 identifies Hophni and Phineas as Eli's corrupt sons.

75660.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75660.question_text: What was the punishment of Ananias and Sapphira for lying to the Holy Spirit?
75660.explanation: Acts 5:1–11 shows both died instantly after lying about the sale of land.

75661.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75661.explanation: Luke 22:61 recalls Peter's triple denial of Jesus.

75662.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75662.explanation: Mark 15:21 states Simon of Cyrene carried Jesus' cross.

75663.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75663.explanation: Pentecost means fifty; it was celebrated 50 days after Passover (Acts 2:1).

75664.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75664.question_text: Who was chosen to replace Judas Iscariot among the apostles?
75664.explanation: Acts 1:26 records that Matthias was chosen by casting lots to replace Judas.

75665.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75665.explanation: Exodus 12 recounts God sparing Israel's firstborns before their deliverance.

75666.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75666.question_text: What does the parable of the ten virgins teach?
75666.explanation: Matthew 25:1–13 teaches about preparedness for the coming of the bridegroom (Christ).

75667.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75667.question_text: Who was the first judge of Israel after Joshua's death?
75667.explanation: Othniel, the son of Kenaz, was the first judge raised by God after Israel cried out due to oppression (Judges 3:9).

75668.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75668.explanation: Exodus 1:9–10 describes Pharaoh's fear of Israel's increasing population.

options.text: He feared they would outnumber and overpower Egypt

75669.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75669.question_text: What was Zechariah's punishment for doubting Gabriel's message?
75669.explanation: Luke 1:20 records Zechariah was struck mute until John the Baptist's birth.

75670.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75670.question_text: Who was stoned for his faith in Acts?

75671.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75671.explanation: Genesis 19:26 says that Lot's wife looked back and she became a pillar of salt.

options.text: She was turned into a pillar of salt
She was swallowed by the earth

75672.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75672.question_text: Which of the following is a fruit of the Spirit?
75672.explanation: Galatians 5 lists love, joy, peace, etc., as the fruit of the Spirit.

75673.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75673.question_text: What did God use to confirm His promise to Abraham?
75673.explanation: In Genesis 15:17, God passed between the pieces of animal sacrifices with a smoking firepot and a flaming torch to seal His covenant.

options.text: A flaming torch and a smoking firepot

75674.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75674.explanation: Isaiah 53 prophesies about the suffering servant, referring to Jesus.

75675.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75675.question_text: What led to the downfall of King Solomon?
75675.explanation: 1 Kings 11:4–8 shows Solomon's heart was turned by his many foreign wives to other gods.

75677.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75677.explanation: Acts 8:26-29 talks about how Phillip baptised the Ethiopian eunuch.

75678.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75678.explanation: Acts 16:16–24 tells of Paul being jailed after casting out a spirit, angering her masters.

75679.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75679.question_text: What sign did God give Gideon to confirm His call?
75679.explanation: Judges 6:36–40 describes Gideon's request for the fleece sign to confirm God's will.

options.text: A wet fleece and dry ground

75680.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
75680.question_text: What role did Nathaniel play in the restoration of Israel?
75680.explanation: Nehemiah led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall and served as governor (Nehemiah 2:17–18).
